Caleb's kin; routs Cushan-Rishathaim of Aram. The land rests 40 years.

300 men with trumpets and torches scatter Midian. The land rests 40 years.

Bears God's covenant with David's house, then confronts him over Bathsheba: 'Thou art the man.'
Solomon's son; his harsh word at Shechem tears ten tribes away. Reigns 17 years.

A good king who tears down idols and is healed of none of his foot disease. Reigns 41 years.
Godly and reforming, but yokes himself to Ahab's house by marriage. Reigns 25 years.
Marries Athaliah of Ahab's line and walks in Israel's ways. Reigns 8 years.
Grandson of Ahab through his mother Athaliah; killed by Jehu in the great purge after one year.
Ahab's daughter murders the royal seed and seizes the throne 6 years — the one break in David's line.
Hidden as an infant by his aunt Jehosheba, crowned at seven by Jehoiada the priest; repairs the Temple, then falls after the priest dies. 40 years.
Defeats Edom, then provokes Israel and is beaten at Beth-shemesh. Reigns 29 years.
A long, strong reign undone when he burns incense unlawfully and is struck with leprosy. 52 years.
Builds and grows mighty because he orders his ways before the LORD. Reigns 16 years.
Sacrifices his son and strips the Temple to buy Assyria's help; Isaiah gives him the Immanuel sign. 16 years.
Cleanses the Temple, defies Assyria and is given 15 added years. Reigns 29 years.
Judah's longest and most wicked reign — 55 years — yet he repents in a Babylonian prison.
Returns to his father's idols; his own servants kill him after 2 years.
The great reformer; the Book of the Law is found in his 18th year. Reigns 31 years, then falls at Megiddo.
Reigns 3 months before Pharaoh Necho carries him to Egypt.
Necho's puppet who burns Jeremiah's scroll; Babylon makes him a vassal. Reigns 11 years.
Reigns 3 months, then is carried to Babylon with the craftsmen and treasures (the first great deportation).
The last king; rebels against Babylon and watches his sons die before his eyes are put out. 11 years to the fall.
First king of the north; sets up golden calves at Bethel and Dan 'lest the people go up to Jerusalem.' 22 years.
Jeroboam's son; struck down by Baasha, ending the first dynasty. 2 years.
Wipes out Jeroboam's house and reigns 24 years in the same sins.
Baasha's son; murdered drunk by his chariot captain Zimri. 2 years.
Reigns 7 days, then burns the palace over himself when Omri closes in.
Founds Samaria as capital and a lasting dynasty; 'did worse than all before him.' 12 years.
Marries Jezebel and enthrones Baal; the great foil of Elijah. 22 years.
Falls through a lattice and sends to Baal-zebub instead of God; dies as Elijah foretold. 2 years.
Ahab's son; slain by Jehu at Naboth's field, ending the house of Omri. 12 years.
Jehu's son; Israel ground down to almost nothing under Aram. 17 years.
Weeps over dying Elisha and wins three victories over Aram. 16 years.
Restores Israel's borders in a long, prosperous, and idolatrous reign — the age of Amos and Hosea. 41 years.
Jehu's line ends in the fourth generation exactly as promised (2 Kings 10:30); after the anarchy that follows Jeroboam II he is slain within six months.
Reigns one month before Menahem cuts him down.
Buys off Assyria's Pul with silver wrung from the land. 10 years.
Menahem's son; killed by his officer Pekah. 2 years.
Allies with Aram against Judah in the Syro-Ephraimite war; loses Galilee and Gilead to Assyria. His 20 years (2 Kings 15:27) overlap the last northern kings before Hoshea conspires and kills him.
The last northern king; his revolt brings Shalmaneser, and after 9 years Samaria falls.
Tears his cloak in twelve pieces to foretell the split, then dooms Jeroboam's house.
Halts Rehoboam's war on the north — 'this thing is from Me' — and later reads Judah Shishak's judgment.
Shuts up heaven three years, calls fire on Carmel, and is taken up in a whirlwind. The great foe of Baal.
Alone against 450 prophets of Baal, he calls down fire and turns the people back: 'The LORD, He is God.'
Alone foretells Ahab's death at Ramoth-gilead against 400 flattering prophets.
Takes up Elijah's mantle and a double portion; heals, raises the dead, and topples kings for 50 years.
The shortest book: Edom is doomed for gloating over fallen Jacob.
Reads a locust plague as the Day of the LORD and foretells the Spirit poured out on all flesh.
Flees his call, is swallowed and spared, then watches Nineveh repent to his dismay.
A herdsman sent north 'two years before the earthquake' to thunder against Israel's ease and injustice.
Marries the unfaithful Gomer as a living parable of the LORD's love for wayward Israel.
Sees the LORD high and lifted up in Uzziah's death-year; prophet of the Holy One and the coming Servant.
Names Bethlehem as the ruler's birthplace and asks only to do justly, love mercy, and walk humbly.
Generations after Jonah spared Nineveh, he pronounces its ruin: the LORD is slow to anger but will not acquit the guilty.
Kinsman of the kings; heralds the Day of the LORD in Josiah's reign and calls Judah to seek meekness.
Called in Josiah's 13th year as 'a prophet to the nations'; weeps over Judah for forty years to the fall.
Wrestles with why God would use Babylon, and is answered: 'the just shall live by his faith.'

event: Jeroboam's golden calves at Bethel & Dan
notes: The north's founding sin: two calves 'lest the people go up to Jerusalem,' a snare to Israel for good.
Anointed to wipe out Baal and the house of Ahab; the LORD grants his line four generations. Reigns 28 years.

event: Elijah and the widow of Zarephath
notes: Through the famine her jar of meal and cruse of oil never fail, and her dead son is raised — mercy to a Gentile in Baal's own country.
Jezebel has Naboth stoned so Ahab can take his vineyard; Elijah pronounces the doom that Jehu will one day execute on this very ground.

event: Elijah taken up in a whirlwind
notes: Fire and horses part the two prophets; Elijah ascends, and Elisha takes up the fallen mantle with a double portion.

event: Naaman the Syrian healed by Elisha
notes: The Aramean commander dips seven times in the Jordan and his leprosy is gone — a sign the God of Israel is God of all.

event: The great earthquake in Uzziah's days
notes: So violent it is remembered for centuries; Amos dates his oracles 'two years' before it.

event: Isaiah gives Ahaz the Immanuel sign
notes: As Aram and Israel besiege Jerusalem, Isaiah promises the faithless king a sign: a virgin shall conceive and bear Immanuel.
He reopens the cleansed Temple and summons all Israel — even the north — to a Passover unmatched since Solomon.
Sick unto death, he turns his face to the wall and weeps; God adds fifteen years and turns the shadow back on the dial.

event: Hezekiah's tunnel to the Siloam pool
notes: Ahead of the siege he cuts an aqueduct through solid rock to bring the Gihon spring inside the walls.
Judah's worst king is dragged to Babylon with hooks; there he humbles himself, and God restores him — the sharpest picture of grace in the monarchy.

event: Huldah the prophetess authenticates the Law
notes: When the lost scroll is found, Josiah's men go to Huldah; she confirms the coming judgment but promises the king will die in peace.
No Passover like it had been kept since the days of the judges — the high point of the last reformation before the fall.
Column by column the king slices the prophet's warnings into the brazier — so Jeremiah dictates them again, with more added.
A shepherd boy with a sling fells the Philistine champion in the Valley of Elah, and Israel's deliverer steps onto the stage.

event: Ruth gleans in the field of Boaz
notes: 'In the days when the judges ruled,' a Moabite widow's loyalty grafts her into Israel — and into the line of David and the Messiah.
A Jerusalem sage's book of wisdom; his grandson's Greek preface (132 BC) is one of the few fixed dates in the silent years.
Josephus first names the three 'schools' of the Jews — the very parties that will fill the pages of the Gospels.
A priestly community withdraws to the Dead Sea to keep the Law and await the LORD; their hidden library surfaces in 1947.
Hyrcanus subdues Edom and compels the Idumeans to be circumcised as Jews — a century later one of them, Herod, will rule as 'King of the Jews.'
The Maccabean high priests now claim the crown as well — priest and king in one house, against the Law's own separation.

event: Alexander Jannaeus rules; Judea at its height
notes: The Hasmonean kingdom reaches its widest borders under a warrior-priest whose cruelty turns the Pharisees against the dynasty.

event: Queen Salome Alexandra reigns in peace
notes: The one Hasmonean queen; she makes peace with the Pharisees — Judea's last calm before Rome.

event: Civil war: Hyrcanus II vs Aristobulus II
notes: The brothers' quarrel over throne and altar draws Pompey's Rome into Judea — the fatal invitation.
On his way to the Parthians who will kill him, the Roman triumvir strips 2,000 talents from the house of God.

event: Antigonus, last Hasmonean king; Parthians take Jerusalem
notes: The Parthians install the last Maccabee on the throne; Herod flees to Rome — and returns with legions and a crown.

event: David anointed by Samuel at Bethlehem
notes: The youngest son, keeping sheep, is anointed in secret — the LORD looks not on the outward appearance but on the heart.

event: Death of Saul and Jonathan at Gilboa
notes: Israel's first king falls on his own sword as the Philistines overrun Mount Gilboa; David laments, 'How are the mighty fallen.'

event: David brings the Ark to Jerusalem
notes: Uzzah dies steadying it, and then it comes up with shouting and trumpets as David dances before the LORD with all his might.
David would build God a house; instead God vows to build David a house — a throne and a Son whose kingdom shall have no end.
The king takes Uriah's wife and hides murder under adultery; Nathan's parable springs the trap — 'Thou art the man.'
David's own son steals the people's hearts and drives him from Jerusalem; the revolt ends with Absalom caught in an oak and a father weeping, 'O Absalom, my son.'

event: David numbers Israel; Araunah's threshing floor
notes: His census brings a plague; where the destroying angel stays his hand, on Araunah's floor, Solomon will one day raise the Temple.

event: Solomon asks for wisdom at Gibeon
notes: Offered anything, the young king asks not for wealth or long life but for a discerning heart — and is given all three.

event: The Queen of Sheba visits Solomon
notes: She comes to test him with hard questions and leaves overwhelmed: the half of his wisdom and glory had not been told her.

event: Solomon's foreign wives turn his heart to idolatry
notes: A thousand wives and concubines draw the wisest man alive into idolatry; for this the LORD will tear ten tribes from his son.
On the Gaza road he baptizes a court official of Ethiopia — the gospel already running toward the ends of the earth.

event: Peter and Cornelius; the gospel opens to the Gentiles
notes: The Spirit falls on a Roman centurion's household still uncircumcised; Peter concludes that God shows no partiality.
In the great mixed church of Antioch the movement is first given the name it will carry ever after.

event: Paul's second journey; the gospel enters Europe
notes: A vision of a man of Macedonia draws Paul across the Aegean to Philippi — the gospel steps onto European soil.
From Corinth he sends the church's earliest surviving letters, steadying young believers on the return of the Lord.
On the eve of his last journey to Jerusalem he sets out the gospel in full to a church he has never seen.
Fourteen storm-tossed nights end on Malta; unharmed by a viper, the prisoner reaches Rome at last.

event: The Synoptic Gospels take written form
notes: Within a generation of the resurrection the eyewitness accounts are set down for the churches.
